Step 1 rewritten to the SINGLE-PATH enhance design (Fabio, 2026-09-08), replacing the toggle design agreed an hour earlier in the same session. One button, one overlay, every model, no per-model branching; the in-graph enhancer is turned OFF rather than kept as a second mode, so Input_enhance_prompt must be forced false on the four graphs - that item is BACK IN SCOPE after being dropped under the toggle design. Fabio's reasoning, recorded because it is the load-bearing part: with a DeepInfra key connected there is no GPU tax on any model, so the free in-graph enhance only ever applied to 4 of 12 models and only on the local path; enhancement becomes its own thing instead of a property of the workflow. Backend is now a SETTING: DeepInfra default (off-GPU, no queue wait), the ComfyUI encoder as the local/uncensored backend on the four eligible models, Ollama for the rest. The ComfyUI encoder was chosen over Ollama for local because it reuses weights the generation already loads while Ollama is a second runtime holding a duplicate copy on the same card (the problem Cubric-Prompt MPI-14 exists for). MEASUREMENT OWED, NOT ASSUMED (step 1d, Fabio's, on the GPU): MPI-35 phase 2's claim that an enhance on qwen3vl_4b_prompt_enhancer evicts the resident generation models was STATIC ANALYSIS WITH NO GPU; the counter-argument is that the encoder is a subset of what the generation already loads. It gates nothing - DeepInfra is the default - but the answer belongs in validation.md. Certain either way: a ComfyUI enhance is a queued job and waits behind a running generation. Also narrowed: MPI-35 phase 2's three worst measured defects on that graph (negative-block welding, the `no ...` clause deleting minimax-h3's overall_soundscape, the 512-token truncation) do NOT reach the four eligible models - krea-2 and flux-2 are not separate-field recipes and minimax-h3 is not eligible - so the overrides are set for future-proofing, not to fix a live defect.

STEP 1a BUILT - Vision now has an LLM client of its own, which is the thing that retires Cubric Prompt. routes/llm.js (GET /llm/status, POST /llm/enhance) holds the DeepInfra key server-side and never returns it; js/services/llmService.js resolves the recipe locally through resolveRecipe -> composeSystemPrompt and picks the backend. VERIFIED LIVE, not claimed: npm test 907/907, lint clean, and a real one-shot call against a server booted on port 3199 returned {ok:true, text:'The lighthouse glowed at dusk.', backend:'ollama', model:'gemma4:e4b'} - honest state comes off the engine's own result, so it names what actually answered. GET /api/ps immediately after returned [], so the keep_alive:0 release in the route's finally really ran: MPI-14's rule now holds on Vision's side too. THREE THINGS A LATER STEP MUST NOT RE-DERIVE. (1) scripts/recipe-engines.mjs MOVED to services/llmEngines.mjs and the old path is a pure re-export, because scripts/ is EXCLUDED from the portable build (scripts/build-portable.mjs:135) - a route importing the backends from there works in dev and is absent in the shipped app. Nothing in the file was edited, so the app and the Stage 1 harness stay on ONE implementation rather than two that drift. (2) Vision ALREADY had the ComfyUI enhance backend: commandRegistry's `promptEnhance` op runs qwen3vl_4b_prompt_enhancer.json with caller-injected injectionParams and returns text via the Output_prompt contract, and MpiBaseFlow._runEnhance is the working precedent. So the comfy backend is a dispatch, not a new engine. (3) The shipped graph leaves use_default_template:True AND hand-rolls its own ChatML, so an injected recipe lands inside the default template's user turn - the opposite of what the Stage 1 harness measures (template off, ChatML hand-rolled). Both are proven on different instruments, so a comfy-backend enhance is NOT the configuration any recipe went green on. Left alone deliberately; it belongs to step 1d's measurement, not to a hunch.
